summary: Redwood AE/SE demoed Console request diagnostics and tracing features focusing on root-cause hunting: request inspector, trace timeline, KV cache visualization, fallback routing and multi-model rollbacks. Customer cares about on-prem/VPC requirements, SSO, and deterministic latency for peak loads. Agreed next steps: send security docs, run dedicated latency pilot, share traces.
transcript:
00:00:00 - Maya Patel: alright everyone thanks for joining, um we'll give a quick intro then jump into the console. we have Connor and Ravi from the SE team with us.
00:00:08 - Tom Reyes: hey thanks, appreciate it. we've been seeing intermittent latency spikes and some weird hallucination-ish outputs in our routing service so wanted to see the debugging flow.
00:00:18 - Maya Patel: perfect, exactly the kind of thing the Request Inspector and trace timeline help with. quick agenda: show trace correlation, request-level logs, KV cache view, and then a simulated failover to show fallback model routing.
00:00:33 - Aisha Khan: quick question, are you demoing hosted or dedicated for this walkthrough? we might need VPC options.
00:00:39 - Connor Liu: good call, we'll demo the Hosted Console first then flip to a Dedicated profile to show differences. note: VPC/private control plane is available for Dedicated, yes.
00:00:50 - Lina Marquez: cool, also want to see how audit logs look for SOC 2 — auditability is a hard req for us.
00:00:56 - Maya Patel: we will cover where audit lines appear in the console and how they tie to request IDs. we'll share the SOC2 pack after.
00:01:05 - (00:01:10) - Connor Liu: ok loading the dashboard now, um— there might be a short lag while I pull the trace index. so at the top is the request inspector search, you can paste a request id, or filter by route, model, time window.
00:01:25 - Derek Wong: i pasted one of our sample IDs in the slack earlier, can you search for 7adf-312b?
00:01:31 - Connor Liu: yeah let me put that in — 7adf-312b — ok results come back, this is interesting, you can see bright red on token latency around token 34 to 42.
00:01:45 - Connor Liu: the timeline shows the latency breakdown — total wall time, model time, queuing, and prefix cache hit ratio. here i can expand the KV cache row and you can see a miss pattern for prefetched prefixes.
00:01:59 - Tom Reyes: miss pattern — could that be our traffic shaping? we do aggressive sharding of keys.
00:02:05 - Ravi Menon: yeah sometimes sharding means prefix distribution is sparse, which hurts prefix caching. also if quantized kernels are chosen that are less friendly to long prefix reuse it can increase model start time.
00:02:18 - Aisha Khan: wait quantized kernels — are we talking about accuracy tradeoffs? what controls the kernel selection?
00:02:24 - Connor Liu: the runtime selects kernels based on model arch and sequence length distribution. in the console Optimize tab there's a recommendation engine that suggests quantization profiles and batch sizes. but you can pin kernels or force fallback to FP16 if you care about quality.
00:02:39 - Derek Wong: ok show us the error analysis for the hallucination case, there's one trace where the output was garbage and the token loss spiked.
00:02:47 - Connor Liu: pulling that trace — here on the right we surface token-level logits and an approximate confidence estimate, it's heuristic not an exact probability. you can see a sudden dip at token 21.
00:02:59 - (00:03:05) - Speaker 1: hmm
00:03:07 - Connor Liu: sometimes that lines up with an upstream prompt truncation or a context split. here there's also a partial prefix cache hit then a miss which forced recompute. that recompute increased both latency and model divergence.
00:03:22 - Tom Reyes: is there a way to replay a trace locally or re-run it against a canary model?
00:03:28 - Connor Liu: yes — replay is in the inspector, you can replay against the same pinned model, a canary, or a smaller guarded variant. i'll show a canary run now; it spawns an isolated execution on Dedicated tester and returns result diff.
00:03:42 - Maya Patel: we'll also show automatic fallback policies — if the canary exceeds token latency threshold it can fallback to a cheaper model or another region. you can configure SLOs per route.
00:03:54 - Lina Marquez: how do you surface cross-request correlation, like when a background job touches same KV keys and causes evictions?
00:04:01 - Connor Liu: good question. we stitch distributed traces by request header and correlation IDs, and in the trace timeline you can toggle 'related requests' to see sibling requests that hit same prefix keys. here's an example: sibling request 7ade-ff0 triggered eviction 5s before the high-latency request.
00:04:18 - Derek Wong: wow that's useful, we suspected a background job. how accurate is the timestamping across regions? we do a multi-region setup.
00:04:25 - Ravi Menon: timestamps are normalized to UTC in the console; for cross-region skew we show clock skew estimates. we don't claim sub-ms perfect sync but it's enough to see causality windows.
00:04:38 - (00:04:45) - Tom Reyes: we run high QPS during morning batch jobs, will the console show aggregation trends?
00:04:51 - Connor Liu: yes the request heatmap and per-route percentile graphs are useful. you can set alerts on p95/p99 and tie them to Slack or PagerDuty.
00:05:02 - Aisha Khan: what about data retention, can we keep raw request logs for 90 days? our compliance team asks for that.
00:05:09 - Maya Patel: retention is configurable per tenant; Dedicated can store longer raw logs in your VPC buckets and you can integrate with your SIEM. we'll include retention config details in the docs pack.
00:05:20 - Derek Wong: great, show the playback feature — can we step through the exact model tokens?
00:05:26 - Connor Liu: yep playback shows token stream and highlights where the runtime switched kernels or hit cache misses. here's an example; see the token timeline at 00:05:40 where kernel swap happens.
00:05:40 - (00:05:45) - Lina Marquez: i see the gray bar saying 'kernel: quantized_v2' then fade to 'kernel: fp16' at that token. is that manual or automatic?
00:05:52 - Connor Liu: automatic unless pinned. runtime may move to a safer path if it detects divergence or quality regression during streaming. You can set a rollback policy per route.
00:06:03 - Tom Reyes: curious about economics — if we run Dedicated for peak, do we still pay per-token? how does billing look?
00:06:11 - Maya Patel: Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commits; usage beyond commit is charged at a discounted overage rate. hosted is pure usage-per-token. We'll send a pricing sketch after this call.
00:06:24 - Derek Wong: and encryption — we need KMS/HSM integration, keys stay in our account.
00:06:30 - Ravi Menon: yes Dedicated supports customer KMS and HSM for runtime keys and you can tie it to your HSM via AWS KMS custom key stores or on-prem HSM connectors. we'll include integration guide.
00:06:42 - (00:06:50) - Connor Liu: ok next i'm going to trigger a simulated model failure to show the fallback path — i'll flip the canary to overslow.
00:06:58 - Connor Liu: done — see the trace — the fallback was triggered at token 12 and the request re-routed to the cheaper model (variant B) with a note in the audit log saying 'fallback: latency-slo-violation'.
00:07:12 - Aisha Khan: how do you avoid inconsistent outputs when fallback happens mid-request? we've had partial completions cause downstream issues.
00:07:19 - Connor Liu: we offer two strategies: optimistic streaming where you accept a delta and de-duplicate at application layer, or enforced atomic fallback that restarts the request on fallback which increases latency but preserves determinism. you can set policy per route.
00:07:35 - Tom Reyes: show me the audit entry for that fallback.
00:07:38 - Connor Liu: here — it includes request id, timestamp, decision reason, prior model id, fallback model id, and the operator id that configured the policy. exportable as JSON.
00:07:49 - Derek Wong: can we get webhook notifications for fallbacks?
00:07:52 - Maya Patel: yes webhooks, plus you can map them to incidents in PagerDuty.
00:07:56 - (00:08:05) - Speaker 2: are there limits to replay?
00:08:08 - Connor Liu: replays can be run against latest snapshots or an archived model binary; for privacy you can scrub PII on import. replays are rate-limited on hosted but unlimited on Dedicated trial tenants.
00:08:22 - Aisha Khan: PII scrubbing — what's exposed in the console if we keep raw logs?
00:08:26 - Ravi Menon: console supports redaction rules; also remote retention control. we recommend encrypting at rest in your VPC and using maskers for sensitive fields.
00:08:37 - (00:08:45) - Lina Marquez: ok show us an end-to-end on a recent incident: we had a spike at 09:12 where a batch job created 20k requests and we saw a 30% p99 increase.
00:08:55 - Connor Liu: loading timeframe — here's the heatmap — p99 spikes immediately after the batch job start. now clicking the anomaly — Console surfaces top contributing routes and correlated requests, ranking by contribution to latency.
00:09:11 - Connor Liu: top contributor is route /nlp/parse-ship which hit a sequence of prefix misses. clicking into a representative request shows the sibling job that evicted cache 7s earlier.
00:09:23 - Derek Wong: that nails it. can console suggest mitigations?
00:09:27 - Connor Liu: yes the Optimize tab will show suggestions like increase prefix window, prewarm cache for batch windows, or adjust autoscale policy to add capacity before batch. it also computes estimated cost delta per suggestion.
00:09:41 - Tom Reyes: how trustworthy are those cost deltas? we need to present to finance.
00:09:45 - Maya Patel: they're estimates based on your historical token mix and our bench profiles; we'll run a dedicated pilot to produce concrete numbers.
00:09:55 - (00:10:00) - Connor Liu: ok i'm going to demo the trace correlation matrix — it's a DAG view showing RPCs and model calls. you can click a node and see outbound requests and latency distribution.
00:10:11 - Aisha Khan: can we export that as SVG for postmortems?
00:10:14 - Connor Liu: yes export to SVG or raw JSON.
00:10:17 - (00:10:25) - Maya Patel: quick pause for questions — anything we haven't covered?
00:10:29 - Lina Marquez: curious if we can integrate with our existing tracing (OpenTelemetry).
00:10:33 - Ravi Menon: absolutely — we ingest spans via OTLP and stitch them to Request Inspector traces using header propagation. there's a short mapping doc we'll share.
00:10:44 - Derek Wong: any limits on how many traces we can keep on hosted?
00:10:47 - Maya Patel: hosted retention is tiered; for long retention we recommend Dedicated with S3 archival.
00:10:55 - (00:11:05) - Tom Reyes: ok show me a failure that's caused by model rollout. we've had a canary ship that regressed quality.
00:11:12 - Connor Liu: pulling a rollout event — here's a canary rollout that increased hallucination rate; Console ties quality regressions to eval sets and alert thresholds. you can open the regression diff and see sample prompts where outputs diverged.
00:11:27 - Aisha Khan: do you run auto-evals on live traffic or a dedicated eval set?
00:11:31 - Connor Liu: both — you can run shadow evals on live traffic and compare outputs against golden prompts in the eval suite. you can also set auto rollback if regression exceeds threshold.
00:11:42 - Derek Wong: is there an SLA for rollbacks? like auto rollback within 5 minutes?
00:11:47 - Maya Patel: rollback timing depends on detection rules and your rollout cadence; we support automated rollback logic but the SLA will be defined in Dedicated contracts.
00:11:59 - (00:12:10) - Connor Liu: ok now i'll show request log search — it's full text and supports fuzzy matching; results highlight tokens and you can jump to exact token time in the playback.
00:12:21 - Lina Marquez: the fuzzy matching could be noisy — is there a way to limit to structured fields?
00:12:25 - Connor Liu: yes you can filter by route, model, status code, latency buckets, and by custom tags you attach to requests.
00:12:34 - Tom Reyes: how do we tag requests from our microservices?
00:12:37 - Ravi Menon: add the redwood-request-id header and optional metadata headers. we have SDKs that auto-instrument popular frameworks.
00:12:45 - (00:12:50) - Maya Patel: i see a quick question from Derek in chat about cryptographic attestation for model binaries.
00:12:56 - Derek Wong: yeah we want to ensure that model artifacts are signed when deployed to Dedicated hosts.
00:13:02 - Raviv Menon: sorry Ravi Menon: yes we support signed artifacts and can integrate with your CI so only signed builds are deployed; we'll send the artifact signing guide.
00:13:11 - (00:13:20) - Connor Liu: ok demoing the playback with a rerun against a pinned FP16 model — you can see the diff pane on the right. note the token-level timing and a small but clear content shift at token 18.
00:13:34 - Aisha Khan: the diff is small but it matters for downstream parsers. any mitigations?
00:13:38 - Connor Liu: you can enforce a strict model pin for that route or use guarded-model variants that run a secondary verifier model to check outputs. there's also post-processing webhooks for normalization.
00:13:50 - (00:14:00) - Tom Reyes: what's the expected ops effort for onboarding Dedicated — like who runs the nodes?
00:14:06 - Maya Patel: Dedicated can be managed by Redwood or run in your private cloud — we offer a managed option where we handle runtime ops and you keep network controls; or you self-host the runtime with our private control plane.
00:14:20 - Derek Wong: for the managed Dedicated, what's the RTO for an incident?
00:14:24 - Maya Patel: SLA depends on plan; we have a premium SLA with <30 min RTO on critical incidents and 24/7 paging for customers on enterprise support.
00:14:36 - (00:14:45) - Lina Marquez: okay can you show an example of a remediation playbook for the exact incident we saw?
00:14:51 - Connor Liu: yes there's a built-in runbook generator — it takes a trace and suggests steps: identify evicting sibling, prewarm cache, roll forward or rollback model, or enable atomic fallback. you can export that as a runbook to your incident tracker.
00:15:08 - Aisha Khan: nice — could we edit templates?
00:15:11 - Connor Liu: fully editable, and templates can be scoped to teams.
00:15:16 - (00:15:25) - Derek Wong: i'm worried about false positives on the autodetectors — we had a detector flip during noisy traffic windows.
00:15:31 - Ravi Menon: detectors are configurable with cooldown windows, minimum sample sizes and weightings to reduce noise-driven actions.
00:15:41 - Tom Reyes: ok let's talk pilot plan — what would you need from us to run a Dedicated latency benchmark?
00:15:47 - Maya Patel: ideally a representative traffic capture, your SLO targets, and a 48–72 hour window to run load tests. Connor will provision a trial tenant.
00:15:58 - Lina Marquez: any infra changes needed on our side? just headers and SSO?
00:16:02 - Maya Patel: mostly headers for correlation and a small NAT rule for outbound, if you choose managed Dedicated we'll do the heavy lifting.
00:16:11 - (00:16:18) - Connor Liu: provisioning the trial... done — created SPK-dedicated-trial-03, credentials emailed to Maya.
00:16:27 - Derek Wong: got it, will try to upload sample traces later tonight.
00:16:31 - (00:16:40) - Maya Patel: quick note on security: we'll send KMS docs and the SOC2 report. we also have FIPS-ready modes if needed.
00:16:48 - Tom Reyes: who should we loop in for legal? procurement?
00:16:52 - Maya Patel: I'll add our Contracts lead, Priya Shah, to the thread after this meeting and include a templated MSA for Dedicated pilots.
00:17:02 - Aisha Khan: any blockers on your side for starting the pilot this week?
00:17:06 - Maya Patel: none, we just need your sample data and to sign the pilot MSA if you want managed Dedicated.
00:17:13 - (00:17:20) - Derek Wong: small nit — can we mask request text in the console for non-admins? we have PII concerns.
00:17:26 - Connor Liu: yep RBAC is granular; you can limit fields per role and mask content for lower-level roles.
00:17:34 - Lina Marquez: ok show me a quick demo of role scoping.
00:17:38 - Ravi Menon: toggling to Admin > Roles — create role 'ops_intern' and restrict view to metadata only — now impersonating to show the interface, they can't see token contents.
00:17:51 - (00:18:00) - Tom Reyes: that's solid. back to the pilot, will you run a 1k qps inc test?
00:18:07 - Connor Liu: yes we can run configurable load windows and simulate cache evictions. we'll capture traces and create a postmortem with cost estimates.
00:18:18 - Derek Wong: what's typical turnaround for that postmortem?
00:18:21 - Maya Patel: 3–5 business days after the test.
00:18:26 - (00:18:35) - Aisha Khan: any known limitations when scaling to burst traffic? we need to respect burstiness.
00:18:40 - Ravi Menon: autoscale is buffer-aware; for Dedicated you can set burst capacity and a warmup threshold to avoid cold kernel swaps. we'll show configuration examples in the follow-up doc.
00:18:54 - Tom Reyes: ok let's talk about integrating with our incident toolchain — we use Slack + PagerDuty + internal JIRA.
00:18:59 - Connor Liu: we have native integrations for Slack and PagerDuty and a webhook for JIRA to open postmortems.
00:19:07 - Maya Patel: small recap: we'll send SOC2/KMS docs, spin up Dedicated trial, run latency benchmark, and Connor will provision the test and return results.
00:19:18 - Derek Wong: sounds good. any other questions?
00:19:22 - Lina Marquez: nothing else here.
00:19:25 - Tom Reyes: no, thanks everyone.
00:19:28 - Maya Patel: quick note — i'll attach a short checklist in the follow-up email for onboarding.
00:19:33 - Connor Liu: one more tip — tag your critical routes with 'no-fallback' during certain windows to avoid inconsistent responses during batch jobs.
00:19:42 - Derek Wong: good tip.
00:19:44 - (00:19:50) - Maya Patel: ok we'll wrap up. thanks for your time. next steps in the calendar invite.
00:19:55 - Tom Reyes: thanks all.
00:20:00 - [call continues: casual chat about logistics and Calendars until 00:48:00 — meeting ends with confirm of next steps and handoffs]
00:48:00 - End of recording.
